title: GuideAI: A Real-time Personalized Learning Solution with Adaptive Interventions
venue: 31st International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI '26)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a key limitation of current LLM-based learning tools: although they can explain concepts and answer questions, they generally do not adapt to learners’ real-time cognitive, attentional, or physiological states. The authors argue that existing AI tutors are too text-centric and reactive, missing opportunities to detect overload, stress, disengagement, or confusion as they occur. To inform the design, they first conducted a formative survey with 66 participants to understand learner needs, preferences, and frustrations with current AI learning systems.

The intervention studied is GuideAI, a web-based personalized learning system that integrates large language models with real-time multi-modal biosensory inputs. GuideAI uses eye tracking, heart rate variability, posture monitoring, and note-taking analysis to infer six learner-state dimensions, including cognitive load, attention, engagement, understanding, stress, and fatigue. Based on these signals, it adapts content, pacing, tone, and modality-specific interventions across text, image, audio, and video learning modes. Adaptive supports include simplifying explanations, restructuring content, redirecting attention, prompting breaks, guiding breathing exercises, and adjusting challenge level.

The empirical evaluation involved a preliminary controlled within-subjects study with 25 participants aged 18 to 42 from undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral backgrounds, all screened to avoid prior knowledge of the learning topics. Each participant used both GuideAI and a non-personalized LLM control condition in a counterbalanced order, with matched STEM-oriented topics and multiple post-task assessments. Outcomes included NASA-TLX cognitive load ratings, multiple-choice recall and problem-solving assessments, subjective ratings, qualitative feedback, and an ablation analysis of intervention types.

The main conclusions are that GuideAI improved both learning performance and user experience relative to the non-adaptive baseline. Participants showed statistically significant gains in problem-solving and some recall measures, alongside lower reported mental demand, effort, and frustration and higher perceived performance. Qualitative feedback suggested that users valued the system’s personalized pacing, stress regulation, and posture reminders. The authors conclude that biosensor-augmented, state-aware LLM learning systems have strong potential to support individualized learning, while also acknowledging important limitations related to privacy, specialized hardware requirements, possible LLM hallucinations, small-sample preliminary validation, and the lack of long-term follow-up.

identified_tools.name: GuideAI
identified_tools.description: A biosensor-augmented, multimodal LLM-based personalized learning system that uses real-time signals such as eye gaze, heart rate variability, posture, and note-taking behavior to infer learner state and adapt content, pacing, tone, and interventions across text, image, audio, and video learning modes.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a real-time adaptive learning platform compared against a non-personalized standard LLM baseline in a within-subjects experiment; it delivered cognitive, physiological, attentional, and tone-adaptive interventions during STEM learning tasks.

findings.finding_summary: In a preliminary within-subjects study, GuideAI improved knowledge performance relative to a non-adaptive LLM baseline across learning modes. Across all modalities, the paper reports a mean improvement of 16.5 percentage points in problem-solving and 10.3 percentage points in recall; problem-solving gains were Text 75% vs 52%, Image 78% vs 48%, Audio 70% vs 59% (p < 0.05), and Video 72% vs 68% (n.s.), while recall gains were Image 82% vs 62% and Audio 70% vs 52% (p < 0.05), with Text 65% vs 64% and Video 72% vs 70%.
findings.measure: Multiple-choice knowledge assessments testing factual recall and conceptual understanding/application-based problems
findings.effect_size: mean improvement of 16.5 percentage points in problem-solving; 10.3 percentage points in recall

findings.finding_summary: GuideAI reduced several NASA-TLX cognitive load dimensions compared with the control condition. Reported differences were lower mental demand (Δ = 0.49, p < 0.05), physical demand (Δ = 0.23, p < 0.05), effort (Δ = 0.28, p < 0.05), and frustration (Δ = 0.54, p < 0.05), alongside higher perceived performance (Δ = 0.34, p < 0.05).
findings.measure: NASA-TLX ratings: mental demand, physical demand, temporal demand, performance, effort, frustration
findings.effect_size: Δ = 0.49 mental demand; Δ = 0.23 physical demand; Δ = 0.28 effort; Δ = 0.54 frustration; Δ = 0.34 performance

findings.finding_summary: Participants rated GuideAI significantly higher than control on focus and attention, content personalization, adaptive pacing, and perceived learning. Means were Focus/Attention M=5.60, SD=1.25 vs 4.85, SD=1.34 (p=0.0418), Content Personalization M=5.55, SD=1.32 vs 4.90, SD=1.26 (p=0.0362), Adaptive Pacing M=5.40, SD=1.28 vs 4.65, SD=1.22 (p=0.0322), and Perceived Learning M=5.50, SD=1.16 vs 4.75, SD=1.18 (p=0.0402).
findings.measure: 7-point Likert ratings of focus and attention, content personalization, adaptive pacing, and perceived learning
findings.effect_size: Focus d=-0.48; Content Personalization d=-0.45; Adaptive Pacing d=-0.47; Perceived Learning d=-0.49

findings.finding_summary: An ablation analysis suggested that GuideAI’s cognitive optimization interventions were the strongest contributors to reduced workload, while attention redirection improved perceived performance and temporal demand. Cognitive optimization reduced mental demand by 0.49 ± 0.10, effort by 0.31 ± 0.08, and frustration by 0.52 ± 0.07; attention redirection reduced temporal demand by 0.39 ± 0.13 and improved perceived performance by 0.49 ± 0.13; tone-adaptive communication most strongly reduced frustration by 0.72 ± 0.11.
findings.measure: NASA-TLX improvement scores by intervention category
findings.effect_size: 0.49 ± 0.10 mental demand; 0.31 ± 0.08 effort; 0.52 ± 0.07 frustration; 0.39 ± 0.13 temporal demand; 0.49 ± 0.13 performance; 0.72 ± 0.11 frustration

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical within-subjects controlled study of a specific system (GuideAI), but it is a preliminary validation with a small sample (n=25), mixed-method reporting, and limited methodological detail for causal credibility. It is stronger than a purely conceptual paper but does not meet blue/green standards for a well-established RCT/QED evidence base.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports comparatively large practical gains, including 16.5 percentage-point average improvement in problem-solving, 10.3 percentage-point improvement in recall, and several statistically significant workload reductions and subjective gains. These results indicate medium-to-large positive impact, even though precision estimates are not reported.
